title: Weight Space Representation Learning on Diverse NeRF Architectures
claim: One encoder maps heterogeneous model representations into a shared latent space that serves multiple downstream tasks regardless of architecture.
layout: 4 stages left-to-right: dashed legend box, encoder, latent blob, brace to tasks
description: A left-to-right framework diagram in four parts. At left, a dashed box shows three NeRF architectures (MLP, tri-plane, hash table), each written as an equation mapping coordinates (x, y, z) through a network or feature grid to outputs (r, g, b, σ). Next, three stacked groups of labeled bars (MLP, tri-plane, hash table) are colored blue, red or green to match a car, a sports car and an airplane in speech bubbles. These feed a large purple trapezoid labeled GMN. The output is a latent-space ellipse where same-object embeddings cluster (blue and red cars together, green airplane apart). A curly brace at right fans the embeddings out to a classifier, k-NN retrieval over a gallery, and an LLM question-answering bubble.
caption: Framework overview. Our representation learning framework leverages a Graph Meta- Network (Lim et al., 2024) encoder to map weights of NeRFs with diverse architectures to a latent space where NeRFs representing similar objects are close to each other, regardless of their architecture. The embeddings are then used as input to downstream pipelines for classification, retrieval, and language tasks.
abstract: Neural Radiance Fields (NeRFs) have emerged as a groundbreaking paradigm for representing 3D objects and scenes by encoding shape and appearance information into the weights of a neural network. Recent studies have demonstrated that these weights can be used as input for frameworks designed to address deep learning tasks; however, such frameworks require NeRFs to adhere to a specific, predefined architecture. In this paper, we introduce the first framework capable of processing NeRFs with diverse architectures and performing inference on architectures unseen at training time. We achieve this by training a Graph Meta-Network within an unsupervised representation learning framework, and show that a contrastive objective is conducive to obtaining an architecture-agnostic latent space. In experiments conducted across 13 NeRF architectures belonging to three families (MLPs, tri-planes, and, for the first time, hash tables), our approach demonstrates robust performance in classification, retrieval, and language tasks involving multiple architectures, even unseen at training time, while also matching or exceeding the results of existing frameworks limited to single architectures. Our code and data are available at https://cvlab-unibo.github.io/gmnerf.
